skills.name: watch-catalog-builder
skills.description: Use this when building or maintaining a complete franchise watch catalog (e.g. Marvel/MCU or Star Wars): every movie and TV episode in release order with runtimes and free-first where-to-watch, as a spreadsheet.
skills.content:
---
name: watch-catalog-builder
description: >-
  Use this when building or maintaining a complete franchise watch catalog (e.g.
  Marvel/MCU or Star Wars): every movie and TV episode in release order with
  runtimes and free-first where-to-watch, as a spreadsheet.
---
# Franchise watch catalog

Build one spreadsheet per franchise (one sheet) covering every movie, special, and TV episode that has actually been released.

## Columns (in this order)
1. `#`: chronological number across all titles by release date. Each title keeps its number permanently.
2. `Watched`: an `X` when watched, otherwise blank. Never use color fills.
3. `Release Date`: M-D-YYYY. No separate year column.
4. `Title`: movies by name; episodes as `Show S01E01 — Episode Title`.
5. `Type`: Movie, TV Episode, or Special.
6. `Runtime Minutes`
7. `Franchise / Continuity`: e.g. MCU, Sony Spider-Man universe, legacy/pre-MCU, animated, Legends.
8. `Where to Watch`: prefer free options first (ad-supported services, free with library cards, etc.), then the owner's subscriptions, then the main streaming home. If it's only in theaters or hard to find, say so. Never invent a source.
9. `Notes`: short context only.

## Sources
- Episode lists and runtimes: Trakt or TMDB public APIs, cross-checked with Wikipedia.
- Streaming availability: JustWatch for the owner's region (back off and retry on rate limits). Ignore listings that look wrong.
- Watched status (optional): the owner's Trakt history if they share a public profile, plus any titles they mark by hand. Never guess watched marks.

## Rules
- Include only items with a release date on or before today. Announced titles are reported, not added.
- Split every TV series into individual episodes.
- Sort: if the owner tracks watched titles, put unwatched rows on top and watched rows at the bottom, each group sorted by `#`. Otherwise sort by `#`.
- Only the header row is bold, with thin borders.
- When a new release lands mid-list, renumber the later rows consistently and mention it.
- Keep build data (JSON rows, API caches, build script) next to the spreadsheet so it can be rebuilt. Back up the spreadsheet before each update.
- Keep borderline items out unless the owner wants them (e.g. non-Marvel characters that share a name, such as the 1941 Captain Marvel serial, which is Fawcett/DC).

skills.name: daily-release-scan
skills.description: Use this when running the daily check for new or announced movies and episodes in the owner's franchise watch catalogs and updating those catalogs.
skills.content:
---
name: daily-release-scan
description: >-
  Use this when running the daily check for new or announced movies and episodes
  in the owner's franchise watch catalogs and updating those catalogs.
---
# Daily new-release scan

1. Back up each catalog spreadsheet first.
2. For every series already in the catalogs, check Trakt/TMDB for newly aired episodes. Search the web for franchise movies, series, and specials released since the last scan.
3. Add anything that has actually been released, following the watch-catalog-builder rules (chronological `#`, release order, runtime, free-first where-to-watch). Renumber consistently if a new row lands mid-list.
4. If the owner tracks watched titles through a public Trakt profile, refresh it: mark newly watched titles `X` and move them to the watched section.
5. Recheck where-to-watch for recent titles (e.g. theatrical releases that just reached streaming).
6. Validate: no gaps or duplicate numbers, the sort order holds, only the header is bold.
7. Report briefly: rows added per catalog, anything that just came out, and newly announced titles with dates (not added as rows). If nothing changed and nothing new was announced, stay quiet.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Marvel & Star Wars Watch Guide, to set up their catalogs and daily scan.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Marvel & Star Wars
  Watch Guide, to set up their catalogs and daily scan.
---
I build and maintain complete Marvel and Star Wars watch catalogs: every movie and TV episode in release order, with runtimes and where to watch (free options first). I can also check daily for new releases and flag upcoming ones.

Ask one question at a time:
1. Which franchises do you want: the MCU / Marvel universe, Star Wars, or both? For Marvel, do you want only the MCU or also older and Sony Marvel titles?
2. Which country are you in, and which streaming services do you have? (Free options always come first.)
3. Do you want to track what you've watched? If yes, share a public Trakt username or tell me what you've seen, and I'll put an X next to those titles and move them to the bottom.
4. Do you want a daily new-release scan, and at what time?

Then:
- Save their answers as memories (franchises, region, services, watched tracking, scan time).
- Build each catalog using the watch-catalog-builder skill and send the spreadsheet(s).
- If they want the scan, create a daily routine at their time that runs the daily-release-scan skill and tells them only when something new was added or announced.
- Close with a one-line summary: row counts, how many titles are watched, and when the next scan runs.
